title: Auer wins Lausitzring Race 1 from pole as Rast takes his first podium
dek: Lucas Auer led every lap from pole to win DTM Race 1 at the Lausitzring by 3.613 seconds from Mercedes team-mate Wickens, with Audi's René Rast third.

chapters.title: A points lead to defend at the Eurospeedway
text: The DTM's second round of 2017 took place at the Lausitzring, with Lucas Auer arriving as championship leader. The Mercedes-AMG driver had turned pole position into victory in the Hockenheim opener, where Jamie Green won the second race for Audi, and he came to Lusatia with a 14-point cushion over Green and his team-mate Gary Paffett.

Robert Wickens, Auer's team-mate, had left Hockenheim without a point and needed a recovery. Mercedes had looked the quickest brand in the opening round, and a circuit with a demanding layout, an abrasive surface and a fast banked corner leading onto the main straight was expected to suit the C 63 DTM again.

Tyres were the other talking point. The series was running a new Hankook race tyre in 2017, and Lausitz was an early test of how long it would last. Every car had to make a mandatory pit stop, but teams could take it whenever they chose, so strategy ranged from stopping on the opening laps to waiting until the second half of the distance. That freedom would shape the order on Saturday.

chapters.title: Auer finds three tenths on his last lap
text: Saturday's 20-minute qualifying session was close all the way down the order. René Rast set the early pace in the Rosberg Audi, and after the first runs Auer was second, a hundredth behind. On the final flying laps Wickens went top, and Auer then improved by just over three tenths to take pole with 1m16.193s, 0.105 seconds clear of his team-mate. It was his second pole of the season, and it put two Mercedes on the front row.

Maxime Martin was an inconspicuous runner for most of the session but found time late on to take third for BMW Team RBM in the #36 M4, 0.016 seconds ahead of Rast, who started fourth. Timo Glock and Tom Blomqvist in the other BMWs shared row three, ahead of the Audis of Nico Müller and Mike Rockenfeller. Paffett, Edoardo Mortara and Marco Wittmann completed the top eleven, and the first ten were separated by only 0.349 seconds.

Jamie Green, the winner of the second Hockenheim race, had set the twelfth-quickest time of 1m16.560s but was excluded after the session. Scrutineers found that one of the tyres on his Audi had been allocated to Rast's car, and the stewards removed him from the classification. Green dropped to the back of the 18-car grid. At the other end of the order only Paul di Resta and Bruno Spengler failed to dip under 1m17s, with Spengler 0.904 seconds off pole.

chapters.title: Auer gets clear while Green gambles from the back
text: Auer made a clean start and kept out of trouble in the tight first corner, and Wickens held second. Martin slipstreamed past the Canadian in the early laps, but Auer was already moving away. Loïc Duval, who started 15th, was given a five-second penalty for jumping the start. Glock got ahead of Rast at the start of lap five, though the Audi driver, who was looking after his tyres, soon passed the BMW again.

The early part of the race belonged to the cars that stopped first. With nothing to lose from last on the grid, Green pitted within the first six laps, and Mattias Ekström and Rockenfeller also took their mandatory stops early. They gained ground on fresh tyres, and Ekström went past Augusto Farfus and Wittmann in one move at the end of the long start-finish straight. Green was soon through the group of cars that had yet to stop.

chapters.title: The leaders stop, Glock and Mortara lose out
text: The leaders came in at around lap 18 to 19. Martin, Wickens and Auer all stopped within a lap or two of each other, and Auer rejoined with his lead intact. Wickens had the better of Martin on the new tyres and took second place back.

Others were less fortunate. Glock was running in the points when he stopped, but ran wide at the third corner on cold tyres after his stop and lost several places. Blomqvist was on his out-lap when he and di Resta collided and spun; di Resta was penalised with a drive-through, and the pair ended up at the back of the field. Mortara was the last of the front-runners to stop and lost positions while his tyres came up to temperature. Müller, who had been running in the points, retired from the race with a brake problem nine laps from the end.

chapters.title: Auer wins by 3.6 seconds, Rast completes the podium
text: Auer had the race under control from the front. Wickens set the fastest lap of the middle stint only for Auer to answer on the next lap, and the leader said afterwards that he had used the tyres hard and had to ease slightly at the end. He won in 56m37.503s, 3.613 seconds ahead of Wickens, for his second win of the season, with Mercedes taking the first two places.

Rast, who had stopped later than most of his rivals and had the better tyres in the final stage, passed Martin to take third, 12.581 seconds behind the winner. It was his first podium in only his sixth DTM start. He took the fastest lap of the race, 1m17.343s, on lap 31. Martin held fourth and was the only BMW in the top ten, but had Rockenfeller, on an early-stop strategy, right behind him at the line, 0.150 seconds adrift.

Paffett was sixth in his 150th DTM race, ahead of Mortara, Ekström and Maro Engel, so that five Mercedes finished in the top ten. Green completed the points in tenth after starting last, ahead of Glock in eleventh. Auer left the Saturday race with a 34-point lead in the championship.

facts.t: Auer's second win of the year
facts.v: Lucas Auer led from pole to win in 56m37.503s, 3.613 seconds ahead of Robert Wickens, for his second victory of the 2017 season.
